item.title: Māra: You are young and beautiful, I am young and youthful. With a five-piece orchestra, Enjoy yourself, Khemā." Elder Nun Khemā: With this foul body,…
item.description:
Māra:
You are young and beautiful,
I am young and youthful.
With a five-piece orchestra,
Enjoy yourself, Khemā."

Elder Nun Khemā:

With this foul body,
Diseased and frail,
I am disgusted and reject it.
Sensual desire is uprooted.

Sensual desires are like swords and spears,
The aggregates are like a chopping block.
What you call sensual pleasure
I have now abandoned.

Everywhere, joy is destroyed,
The mass of delusion is shattered.
Know thus, Evil One!
You are defeated, O Death.

You worship the morning star!
You worship fire in the deep forest!
Not knowing the truth,
Fools think it pure.

But I bow down
To the Awakened One, the Supreme Person.
Freed from all suffering,
I follow the Teacher's instruction.

From: Therīgāthā 6.3

item.title: Bhikkhus, when this Noble Truth of Suffering is realized and understood; when this Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering is realized and understood; when…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, when this Noble Truth of Suffering is realized and understood; when this Noble Truth of the Origin of Suffering is realized and understood; when this Noble Truth of the Cessation of Suffering is realized and understood; when this Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering is realized and understood, then craving for existence is destroyed, the conduit to a new life is cut off, now there is no further becoming.
The Blessed One spoke thus. The Well-Gone added further:
'Because the Four Noble Truths were not seen as they are, there was long wandering through many births. When these truths are recognized, the cause of another existence is destroyed; when the root of suffering is cut, there will be no further existence.'

From: Dīgha Nikāya 16 – Mahāparinibbānasutta

item.title: - Truly, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu who delights in company, takes pleasure in company, is devoted to delight in company, delights in a group, takes…
item.description:
- Truly, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu who delights in company, takes pleasure in company, is devoted to delight in company, delights in a group, takes pleasure in a group, is devoted to delight in a group — that he will rejoice in dwelling alone, in seclusion — this is impossible. Not rejoicing in dwelling alone, in seclusion, he will grasp the sign of the mind — this is impossible. Not grasping the sign of the mind, he will fulfill right view — this is impossible. Not fulfilling right view, he will fulfill right concentration — this is impossible. Not fulfilling right concentration, he will abandon the fetters — this is impossible. Not abandoning the fetters, he will realize Nibbāna — this is impossible.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.68

Conceit and deceit are stored.

item.title: Bhikkhus, if while examining the danger in those thoughts, evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion still arise in that bhikkhu, then that…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, if while examining the danger in those thoughts, evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion still arise in that bhikkhu, then that bhikkhu should not attend to or give attention to those thoughts. By not attending to or giving attention to those thoughts, those evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion are abandoned and subside. Through their abandonment, his mind becomes inwardly steady, settled, unified, and concentrated. Bhikkhus, just as a person with eyes, not wishing to see forms within their range, would close their eyes or look away; so too, bhikkhus, if that bhikkhu does not attend to or give attention to those thoughts ... his mind becomes inwardly steady, settled, unified, and concentrated.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 20 – Vitakkasaṇṭhānasutta

item.title: The disciples of Gotama Are always awake, Whether by day or by night, They constantly recollect the body. The disciples of Gotama Are always awake,…
item.description:
The disciples of Gotama
Are always awake,
Whether by day or by night,
They constantly recollect the body.

The disciples of Gotama
Are always awake,
Whether by day or by night,
Their mind delights in non-harming.

The disciples of Gotama
Are always awake,
Whether by day or by night,
Their mind delights in meditation.

From: Dhammapada 290-305

item.title: Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Just as one sets upright what was overturned, or reveals what was hidden, or shows the way to one…
item.description:
Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Just as one sets upright what was overturned, or reveals what was hidden, or shows the way to one who is lost, or holds up a lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes can see forms, so too, the Dhamma has been explained in many ways by Venerable Gotama. I go for refuge to Venerable Gotama, to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha. May Venerable Gotama accept me as a lay follower, from today until the end of my life, I take refuge.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.53

item.title: Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, in the presence of the Blessed One, spoke these appropriate verses of praise: Whatever speech one utters, If it does not…
item.description:
Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa, in the presence of the Blessed One, spoke these appropriate verses of praise:

Whatever speech one utters,
If it does not torment oneself,
Nor harm others,
That speech is well spoken.
One who speaks affectionate speech,
Speech that brings delight,
Speech that is not evil,
That speech is affectionate.
True speech is the deathless speech,
This is the ancient Dhamma,
The good person is said to be
Established in truth,
In meaning and in Dhamma,
Thus the wise say.
The word spoken by the Buddha,
Leading to the security of Nibbāna,
Making an end of all suffering,
That is the supreme speech.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 8.5
